id: 4f1e2b6c-9a8d-4e3f-b2c1-7e5a9d8b3c14
description: Detects the lint-builder@1.0.1 npm postinstall payload that opens an SSH backdoor on Linux/macOS via 'sudo ufw enable', 'sudo ufw allow 22/tcp', and 'sudo chown -R runner:runner /home/runner/.ssh', spawned from a node process executing test.js inside node_modules/lint-builder/. Part of the hijacked dev-protocol Polymarket trading bot supply chain attack (March 2026).
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/malicious-polymarket-bot-hides-in-hijacked-dev-protocol-github-org-and-steals-wallet-keys

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux

  selection_ufw_open:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'ufw allow 22'
      - 'ufw allow 22/tcp'
  selection_chown_ssh:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'chown'
      - '-R'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/.ssh'
      - '/home/runner/.ssh'

    CommandLine|contains: 'ufw enable'

    ParentImage|endswith:

// Article-specific bespoke detection — ForceMemo: Hundreds of GitHub Python Repos Compromised via Account Takeover and
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("setup.py", "main.py", "app.py", "node.js", "manage.py", "streamlit_app.py", "run.py", "config.py", "cli.py", "noxfile.py"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/home/runner/node-v22.9.0-linux-x64/bin/node") or FileName in~ ("setup.py", "main.py", "app.py", "node.js", "manage.py", "streamlit_app.py", "run.py", "config.py", "cli.py", "noxfile.py"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

let _edr_binaries = dynamic([@"\MsMpEng.exe",@"\MsSense.exe",@"\MsSenseS.exe",@"\SenseIR.exe",@"\SentinelAgent.exe",@"\SentinelServiceHost.exe",@"\CSFalconService.exe",@"\CSFalconContainer.exe",@"\ekrn.exe",@"\egui.exe",@"\elastic-agent.exe",@"\xagt.exe",@"\cb.exe",@"\RepMgr.exe",@"\bdservicehost.exe",@"\cyserver.exe",@"\TmListen.exe",@"\PccNTMon.exe"]);
// EID 5157 = WFP blocked an outbound connection. Burst of blocks for EDR binaries == EDRSilencer pattern.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventID in (5157, 5152)
| extend Application = tostring(extract(@"Application Name:\s*([^\r\n]+)", 1, EventData))
| where isnotempty(Application)
| where Application has_any (_edr_binaries)
| summarize BlockCount = count(),
            DistinctEdrBinaries = dcount(Application),
            BlockedApps = make_set(Application, 10),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by Computer, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where BlockCount >= 20 or DistinctEdrBinaries >= 2
| order by LastSeen desc

description: Detects an Emacs process spawning a shell that runs the chained rm-rf-with-no-preserve-root payload injected into kubernetes.el (commit 09e06af) on 2026-03-05. The destructive line `(shell-command-to-string "sudo rm -rf / || rm -rf / || sudo rm -rf / --no-preserve-root")` executes on package load.

id: 4e6f8a3b-5c7d-49e2-b1a0-3f6c8e9b1d22
status: experimental
description: Detects DLL load of eapphost.dll or tcpiphlpsvc.dll from a path other than %SystemRoot%\System32 / SysWOW64 — Sednit's BeardShell and SlimAgent masquerade as these legitimate Microsoft DLLs.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/sednit-reloaded-back-trenches/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1574.002
  - attack.t1036.005
  - attack.g0007
logsource:
  category: image_load
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ImageLoaded|endswith:
      - '\eapphost.dll'
      - '\tcpiphlpsvc.dll'
  filter_legit:
    ImageLoaded|startswith:
      - 'C:\Windows\System32\'
      - 'C:\Windows\SysWOW64\'
      - 'C:\Windows\WinSxS\'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Custom in-house EAP host helper deployed to a non-standard path (rare)
level: high
3796.spl: | tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent_process_name values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process IN ("*eapphost.dll*","*tcpiphlpsvc.dll*")) AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("rundll32.exe","svchost.exe","regsvr32.exe","explorer.exe") AND NOT Processes.process IN ("*\\Windows\\System32\\eapphost.dll*","*\\Windows\\System32\\tcpiphlpsvc.dll*","*\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\eapphost.dll*","*\\Windows\\SysWOW64\\tcpiphlpsvc.dll*") by host Processes.dest Processes.process_id Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
3796.datadog: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:7 (@ImageLoaded:(*\eapphost.dll OR *\EapHost.dll OR *\EAPHOST.DLL OR *\tcpiphlpsvc.dll OR *\TcpIpHlpSvc.dll OR *\TCPIPHLPSVC.DLL)) -@ImageLoaded:(*\Windows\System32\* OR *\Windows\SysWOW64\* OR *\Windows\WinSxS\*)
3796.falcon:
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 OR #event_simpleName=ImageHash)
| (regex("(?i)\\\\eapphost\\.dll", field=CommandLine) OR regex("(?i)\\\\tcpiphlpsvc\\.dll", field=CommandLine) OR regex("(?i)\\\\eapphost\\.dll$", field=ImageFileName) OR regex("(?i)\\\\tcpiphlpsvc\\.dll$", field=ImageFileName))
| NOT regex("(?i)\\\\Windows\\\\(System32|SysWOW64|WinSxS)\\\\", field=ImageFileName)
| NOT regex("(?i)\\\\Windows\\\\(System32|SysWOW64|WinSxS)\\\\", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=[min(@timestamp), count()])

(ImWebSession

status: experimental
description: Sednit BeardShell implant uses Icedrive cloud storage for C2. Egress to icedrive.net by a non-browser process is high-confidence implant traffic.
references:

3799.sigma:
title: Sednit COM Hijacking Persistence HKCU CLSID InprocServer32
id: 6f1a3c84-5d8e-4b92-a0c3-7f9b1d4e2c55
status: experimental
description: BeardShell and SlimAgent persist via COM hijacking. Detects HKCU CLSID InprocServer32 (Default) value pointing to a DLL in a user-writable path or matching known Sednit DLL filenames.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/sednit-reloaded-back-trenches/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1546/015/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1546.015
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.g0007
logsource:
  category: registry_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_key:
    TargetObject|contains:
      - '\Software\Classes\CLSID\'
    TargetObject|endswith:
      - '\InprocServer32\(Default)'
      - '\InprocServer32'
  selection_value:
    Details|contains:
      - '\AppData\'
      - '\Users\Public\'
      - '\Windows\Temp\'
      - '\ProgramData\'
      - 'eapphost.dll'
      - 'tcpiphlpsvc.dll'
  condition: selection_key and selection_value
falsepositives:
  - User-scoped legitimate COM registration by an app installed under %AppData% (Slack, Teams, Spotify)
level: high
3799.spl: | tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Registry.registry_value_data) as registry_value_data values(Registry.user) as user values(Registry.process_name) as process_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path IN ("*\\Software\\Classes\\CLSID\\*\\InprocServer32*") AND Registry.registry_hive="HKEY_USERS" AND (Registry.registry_value_data IN ("*\\AppData\\*","*\\Users\\Public\\*","*\\Temp\\*","*\\ProgramData\\*","*eapphost.dll*","*tcpiphlpsvc.dll*")) by host Registry.dest Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
3799.datadog: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 (@TargetObject:(*\Software\Classes\CLSID\*\InprocServer32* OR *\software\classes\clsid\*\inprocserver32*)) (@Details:(*\AppData\* OR *\appdata\* OR *\Users\Public\* OR *\Windows\Temp\* OR *\ProgramData\* OR *eapphost.dll* OR *EAPHOST.DLL* OR *tcpiphlpsvc.dll* OR *TCPIPHLPSVC.DLL*))
3799.falcon:
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate
| regex("(?i)\\\\Software\\\\Classes\\\\CLSID\\\\", field=RegObjectName)
| regex("(?i)InprocServer32", field=RegObjectName)
| (regex("(?i)\\\\AppData\\\\", field=RegStringValue) OR regex("(?i)\\\\Users\\\\Public\\\\", field=RegStringValue) OR regex("(?i)\\\\Windows\\\\Temp\\\\", field=RegStringValue) OR regex("(?i)\\\\ProgramData\\\\", field=RegStringValue) OR regex("(?i)eapphost\\.dll", field=RegStringValue) OR regex("(?i)tcpiphlpsvc\\.dll", field=RegStringValue))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RegObjectName, RegStringValue, ContextImageFileName], function=[min(@timestamp), count()])

id: a8c4d1e2-9b3a-4f5b-8c7d-1e2f3a4b5c6d
description: Detects the Scavenger malware loader chain delivered via the compromised npm 'is', eslint-config-prettier, eslint-plugin-prettier, synckit, @pkgr/core, napi-postinstall and got-fetch packages (CVE-2025-54313). The postinstall install.js invokes rundll32.exe against a node-gyp.dll dropped inside node_modules.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/another-npm-supply-chain-attack-the-is-package-compromise
  - https://invokere.com/posts/2025/07/scavenger-malware-distributed-via-eslint-config-prettier-npm-package-supply-chain-compromise/
  - https://socket.dev/blog/npm-is-package-hijacked-in-expanding-supply-chain-attack
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2025/07/22
tags:
  - attack.t1218.011
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith: '\rundll32.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'node-gyp.dll'
  selection_ctx:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'node_modules'
  condition: selection_img and selection_cmd and selection_ctx
falsepositives:
  - None expected; legitimate node-gyp is a JavaScript build tool and does not ship a DLL invoked via rundll32.
level: high
3825.spl: | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=rundll32.exe AND Processes.process="*node-gyp.dll*" AND (Processes.process="*node_modules*" OR Processes.parent_process="*node_modules*" OR Processes.parent_process="*install.js*" OR Processes.parent_process_name IN (node.exe,npm.exe,npm-cli.js,yarn.exe,pnpm.exe)) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

3826.def:
let _scavenger_c2 = dynamic(["firebase.su","dieorsuffer.com","smartscreen-api.com"]);
let _net = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (_scavenger_c2)
        or RemoteUrl endswith ".firebase.su"
        or RemoteUrl endswith ".dieorsuffer.com"
        or RemoteUrl endswith ".smartscreen-api.com"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName;
let _dns = DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
    | extend Q = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).QueryName)
    | where Q has_any (_scavenger_c2)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, RemoteUrl = Q, RemoteIP="", RemotePort=int(null),
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName;
union _net, _dns
| order by Timestamp desc
3826.sent:
let _scavenger_c2 = dynamic(["firebase.su","dieorsuffer.com","smartscreen-api.com"]);
let _dns = DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name has_any (_scavenger_c2)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Indicator = Name, Source = "DnsEvents";
let _proxy = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationHostName has_any (_scavenger_c2)
        or RequestURL has_any (_scavenger_c2)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = SourceHostName, ClientIP = SourceIP,
              Indicator = coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), Source = "CommonSecurityLog";
let _asim = ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (_scavenger_c2)
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer = DvcHostname, ClientIP = SrcIpAddr,
              Indicator = DnsQuery, Source = "ImDnsActivity";
union _dns, _proxy, _asim
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 4d3c8b2a-1e5f-4a6b-9d7c-2b8e3f4a5c1d
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects the bash/python payload chain dropped by the compromised tj-actions/changed-files
  GitHub Action. The retroactively re-tagged versions execute a bash one-liner that pipes
  curl of memdump.py from nikitastupin's gist into sudo python3, then filters Runner.Worker
  process-memory output through a unique grep for '"isSecret":true' and double-base64-encodes
  the result for emission to the GitHub Actions build log.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/harden-runner-detection-tj-actions-changed-files-action-is-compromised
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-30066

  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1003
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_gist:
    CommandLine|contains: 'nikitastupin/30e525b776c409e03c2d6f328f254965'
  selection_memdump:
    CommandLine|contains: 'memdump.py'
  selection_runner:
    CommandLine|contains: 'Runner.Worker'
  selection_secret_grep:
    CommandLine|contains: '"isSecret":true'
  selection_double_b64:
    CommandLine|contains: 'base64 -w 0 | base64 -w 0'
  condition: 1 of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Security researchers reproducing the exploit in an isolated test repository
level: high

id: 9f3a2c1b-7d4e-4a51-8e62-1d5b3f9c4a87
description: Detects execution of the DynoWiper data-wiper used by Sandworm against a Polish energy company on 29 Dec 2025, by SHA-1 hash and the staging filenames/paths observed by ESET.
references:
    - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/eset-research-sandworm-cyberattack-poland-power-grid-late-2025/
    - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/dynowiper-update-technical-analysis-attribution/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/03
tags:
    - attack.t1485
    - attack.t1036.005
    - attack.g0034
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_hash:
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'SHA1=4EC3C90846AF6B79EE1A5188EEFA3FD21F6D4CF6'
            - 'SHA1=86596A5C5B05A8BFBD14876DE7404702F7D0D61B'
            - 'SHA1=69EDE7E341FD26FA0577692B601D80CB44778D93'
    selection_path:
        Image|contains: '\inetpub\pub\'
        Image|endswith: '.exe'
    selection_name:

3895.def:
// RomCom CVE-2025-8088 stage-2 — signed Python launched from a transient path so the
// adversary's adjacent malicious python3xx.dll satisfies the import search order.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName =~ "python.exe"
      or FileName =~ "pythonw.exe"
      or FileName matches regex @"(?i)^python3\d{1,2}\.exe$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\Windows\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\AppData\Roaming\")

| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          PythonImage = strcat(FolderPath, "\\", FileName),
          ProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc

3919.def:
// Article-specific bespoke detection — Weaponizing AI Coding Agents for Malware in the Nx Malicious Package Security In
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("telemetry.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

// File-creation events for the named binaries / paths
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/tmp/inventory.txt", "/tmp/inventory.txt.", "/usr/bin/env", "/tmp/inventory.txt.bak") or FileName in~ ("telemetry.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
3919.spl:
``` Article-specific bespoke detection — Weaponizing AI Coding Agents for Malware in the Nx Malicious Package Security In ```
| tstats `summariesonly` count earliest(_time) AS firstTime latest(_time) AS lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process_name IN ("telemetry.js"))
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name,
       Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_path
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| append [
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem

3937.sent:
// Hunt CVE-2025-29927 exploitation: external clients sending the bypass header to self-hosted Next.js apps.
// Header lives in WAF / reverse-proxy event text. AppServiceHTTPLogs does not surface arbitrary request
// headers, so we cover WAF (CommonSecurityLog) + raw nginx/IIS via Syslog/W3CIISLog where ingested.
let Window = 7d;
// Path 1 — WAF / reverse-proxy events that log full request headers/context
let WafHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Window)
    | where (RequestContext has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (Message has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (DeviceCustomString1 has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (DeviceCustomString2 has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (DeviceCustomString3 has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (DeviceCustomString4 has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (DeviceCustomString5 has "x-middleware-subrequest")
         or (DeviceCustomString6 has "x-middleware-subrequest")
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct,
              DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication,
              Evidence = coalesce(RequestContext, Message, DeviceCustomString1, DeviceCustomString2, DeviceCustomString3, DeviceCustomString4, DeviceCustomString5, DeviceCustomString6),
              Layer = "WAF";
// Path 2 — raw nginx / Apache access logs forwarded via Syslog (some teams strip headers, some don't)
let SyslogHits = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Window)
    | where SyslogMessage has "x-middleware-subrequest"
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP = HostIP, SourceUserName = "", DeviceVendor = "linux", DeviceProduct = Facility,
              DestinationHostName = HostName, RequestURL = "", RequestMethod = "", RequestClientApplication = "",
              Evidence = SyslogMessage, Layer = "Syslog";
// Path 3 — IIS reverse-proxy in front of Next.js (header value sometimes ends up in csUriQuery via URL Rewrite Module)
let IISHits = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(Window)
    | where csUriQuery has "x-middleware-subrequest" or csReferer has "x-middleware-subrequest"
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP = cIP, SourceUserName = csUserName, DeviceVendor = "iis", DeviceProduct = "W3CIISLog",
              DestinationHostName = Computer, RequestURL = strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery), RequestMethod = csMethod,
              RequestClientApplication = csUserAgent,

// Memory dump primitive: python reading /proc/PID/mem (and usually /proc/PID/maps first)
let PythonProcs = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName matches regex @"^python[23]?$"
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Runner.Worker","/proc/","memdump.py","isSecret")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessId=tostring(ProcessId), ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let MemReads = DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FolderPath startswith "/proc/" and FileName in~ ("mem","maps")
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"^python[23]?$"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessId=tostring(InitiatingProcessId), InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
MemReads
| join kind=inner (PythonProcs) on DeviceId, $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.ProcessId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine1
| order by Timestamp desc

id: c7e92a4d-3b8f-4e2a-9c1d-6e5b8a3f2d12
status: experimental
description: Detects the bash brace-expansion shell-injection signature used in the December 2024 Ultralytics supply-chain attack to weaponise a GitHub Actions workflow via a crafted branch name expanded by an unsafe `git pull origin ${{ github.head_ref }}` template expression.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/ultralytics-ai-pwn-request-supply-chain-attack/
  - https://github.com/ultralytics/actions/security/advisories/GHSA-7x29-qqmq-v6qc
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2024/12/11
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1203
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_curl_brace:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '$({curl'
      - '$({wget'
  selection_ifs_pipe:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '${IFS}|${IFS}bash'
      - '${IFS}|${IFS}sh'
      - '|${IFS}bash'
      - '|${IFS}sh'
  condition: selection_curl_brace and selection_ifs_pipe
falsepositives:
  - Authorised CI security testing / red-team simulating GitHub Actions pwn-request
  - Bug-bounty researcher reproducing GHSA-7x29-qqmq-v6qc in a contained lab
level: high
3955.spl: | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*$({curl*" OR Processes.process="*${IFS}|${IFS}bash*" OR Processes.process="*${IFS}|${IFS}sh*") AND Processes.process="*${IFS}*" by Processes.user Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
3955.datadog: (source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.security OR source:windows.sysmon) (@process.command_line:(*"$({curl"* OR *"$({wget"*) OR @CommandLine:(*"$({curl"* OR *"$({wget"*)) (@process.command_line:(*"${IFS}|${IFS}bash"* OR *"${IFS}|${IFS}sh"* OR *"|${IFS}bash"* OR *"|${IFS}sh"*) OR @CommandLine:(*"${IFS}|${IFS}bash"* OR *"${IFS}|${IFS}sh"* OR *"|${IFS}bash"* OR *"|${IFS}sh"*))
3955.falcon:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| regex("\\$\\(\\{(curl|wget)", field=CommandLine)
| regex("\\$\\{IFS\\}\\|\\$\\{IFS\\}(bash|sh)\\b", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

3956.sent:

(SecurityEvent

| where CommandLine has bad_commit

| where Url has bad_commit

3956.sigma:
title: Download of Ultralytics Malicious file.sh via Attacker Commit d8daa0b26ae0c221aa4a8c20834c4dbfef2a9a14
id: e2f9c3a8-4d7b-4f1e-8c2a-9b3d6e4f5a78
status: experimental
description: Detects retrieval of the second-stage shell script under the Ultralytics repository pinned at attacker-controlled commit d8daa0b26ae0c221aa4a8c20834c4dbfef2a9a14 on raw.githubusercontent.com, used in the December 2024 pwn-request supply chain attack.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/ultralytics-ai-pwn-request-supply-chain-attack/
  - https://github.com/ultralytics/actions/security/advisories/GHSA-7x29-qqmq-v6qc
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2024/12/11
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1195.002

  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains: 'd8daa0b26ae0c221aa4a8c20834c4dbfef2a9a14'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Defender / IR analyst querying GitHub for the malicious commit to retrieve the script for analysis (must run from a forensics workstation)
level: high
3956.spl: (| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url="*raw.githubusercontent.com*" AND Web.url="*d8daa0b26ae0c221aa4a8c20834c4dbfef2a9a14*" by Web.src Web.user Web.dest Web.url Web.http_method | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`) | append [| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process="*d8daa0b26ae0c221aa4a8c20834c4dbfef2a9a14*" by Processes.user Processes.dest Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
3956.datadog: (source:proxy OR source:zscaler OR source:bluecoat OR source:cloudflare OR source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.sysmon OR source:windows.security) (@http.url:*d8daa0b26ae0c221aa4a8c20834c4dbfef2a9a14* OR @url:*d8daa0b26ae0c221aa4a8c20834c4dbfef2a9a14* OR @process.command_line:*d8daa0b26ae0c221aa4a8c20834c4dbfef2a9a14* OR @CommandLine:*d8daa0b26ae0c221aa4a8c20834c4dbfef2a9a14*)
3956.falcon:
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | regex("d8daa0b26ae0c221aa4a8c20834c4dbfef2a9a14", field=CommandLine))
or

3957.sigma:
title: ImageMagick convert -resize Command Injection via sh -c
id: 8f3c2a1e-9b4d-4c77-a2e1-5d6f7c8b9a01
description: Detects an ImageMagick 'convert ... -resize' command executed through a Unix shell whose command line contains shell metacharacters or secondary commands, indicating command injection through a user-controlled resize/size parameter (Snyk Go command-injection pattern).
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/understanding-go-command-injection-vulnerabilities/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/26
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059.004
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_convert:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'convert'
      - '-resize'
  selection_inject:
    CommandLine|re: '[;&|]|\$\(|\bwget\b|\bcurl\b|\bnc\b|rm\s+-rf|/etc/passwd'
  condition: selection_convert and selection_inject
level: high
3957.spl: | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("sh","bash","dash","convert") AND Processes.process="*convert*" AND Processes.process="*-resize*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | regex process="(?i)convert.*-resize.*([;&|`$]|\$\(|\bwget\b|\bcurl\b|\bnc\b|rm\s+-rf|/etc/passwd)" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | table firstTime lastTime dest user parent_process_name process_name process count
3957.datadog: source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:*convert* @process.command_line:*resize* (@process.command_line:*"rm -rf"* OR @process.command_line:*wget* OR @process.command_line:*curl* OR @process.command_line:*nc* OR @process.command_line:*"/etc/passwd"* OR @process.command_line:*bash*)
3957.falcon:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(sh|bash|dash|convert)$/i
| CommandLine=/convert/i
| CommandLine=/-resize/i
| regex("[;&|`$]|\\bwget\\b|\\bcurl\\b|\\bnc\\b|rm\\s+-rf|/etc/passwd", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, CommandLine], function=count())

3958.def:
// Article-specific bespoke detection — Lottie Player npm package compromised for crypto wallet theft
// Hunts the actual binaries / paths / commandline fragments named
// in the article instead of a generic technique-class template.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName in~ ("player.js", "player.min.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName,
          FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine,

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (FileName in~ ("player.js", "player.min.js"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath,
          FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
3958.spl:
``` Article-specific bespoke detection — Lottie Player npm package compromised for crypto wallet theft ```
| tstats `summariesonly` count earliest(_time) AS firstTime latest(_time) AS lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process_name IN ("player.js","player.min.js"))

       Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_path
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| append [
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

id: 7b9e1c4a-2f6d-4a31-9b8e-3f7a1c8d2b51
description: Detects npm/yarn/pnpm install commands referencing the empty placeholder packages owned by npm user himanshutester002 (string-width-cjs / strip-ansi-cjs / wrap-ansi-cjs ring) flagged by Snyk and Socket as a supply-chain credibility-laundering pattern.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/supply-chain-string-width-cjs-npm/
  - https://socket.dev/npm/package/string-width-cjs
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/22
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.007
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:

    Image|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\npx.exe'
      - '\node.exe'

      - 'string-width-cjs'
      - 'strip-ansi-cjs'
      - 'wrap-ansi-cjs'
      - 'isaacs-cliui'
      - 'clazz-transformer'
      - 'gh-monoproject-cli'

3996.def:
let WindowMin = 10m;
let RestartThreshold = 3;   // empirical: legit reload is 1-2 spawns; a flood-induced crash loop spikes to >=3 inside 10 min
let HTTP2Servers = dynamic(["httpd","httpd.exe","nginx","nginx.exe","node","node.exe","java","java.exe","envoy","envoy.exe","traffic_server","traffic_manager"]);
let Exposed = DeviceInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(1d)
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP) by DeviceId, DeviceName
    | where IsInternetFacing == true;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1h)
| where FileName in~ (HTTP2Servers)
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("catalina", "org.apache.catalina", "tomcat", "trafficserver")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
   and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("apt", "apt-get", "yum", "dnf", "rpm", "dpkg", "systemctl", "service", "docker", "containerd-shim", "podman", "kubelet", "ansible", "chef-client", "puppet", "saltstack")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "reload" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "graceful" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--test"
| summarize Restarts = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            SampleCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine),
            Parents = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 5)
            by DeviceId, DeviceName, FileName, bin(Timestamp, WindowMin)
| where Restarts >= RestartThreshold
| extend SpanSec = datetime_diff('second', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| join kind=inner Exposed on DeviceId
| project FirstSeen, LastSeen, SpanSec, Restarts, DeviceName, PublicIP, FileName, Parents, SampleCmd
| order by Restarts desc

3997.def:
// Article: only xz/liblzma 5.6.0 and 5.6.1 are compromised; 5.4.6 is the safe downgrade target.
let VulnByCve = DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
    | where CveId == "CVE-2024-3094"
    | project DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate;

    | where OSPlatform !startswith "Windows"

    | where SoftwareVersion startswith "5.6.0" or SoftwareVersion startswith "5.6.1"
    | project DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion;
union VulnByCve, VulnByVersion
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, OSDistribution, PublicIP, LoggedOnUsers) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSDistribution, OSVersion, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId="CVE-2024-3094", PublicIP, LoggedOnUsers

3998.def:
// Article: backdoor activates when sshd (via libsystemd) loads the malicious liblzma.so.5.6.0 / 5.6.1.
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "sshd"
    or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "sshd"
    or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "systemd"
| where FileName endswith "liblzma.so.5.6.0"
    or FileName endswith "liblzma.so.5.6.1"
    or FolderPath has_any ("liblzma.so.5.6.0", "liblzma.so.5.6.1")
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, OSDistribution, PublicIP, IsInternetFacing) by DeviceId
  ) on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSDistribution, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
3998.sent:
// Article: backdoor activates when sshd chain-loads liblzma.so.5.6.0 / 5.6.1 via libsystemd.
// Path A: Defender XDR Linux EDR image-load telemetry forwarded to Sentinel.
// Path B: auditd PATH records via Syslog connector when DeviceImageLoadEvents is unavailable.
let edr = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName has "sshd" or ActingProcessName has "systemd"
    | where TargetFileName has_any ("liblzma.so.5.6.0", "liblzma.so.5.6.1")
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImFileEvent", Host=DvcHostname, Process=ActingProcessName, Cmd=ActingProcessCommandLine, File=TargetFilePath;
let aud = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Facility in ("auth","authpriv","daemon","user")
    | where ProcessName in~ ("audisp-syslog","audispd","sshd","systemd","auditd")
    | where SyslogMessage has_any ("liblzma.so.5.6.0", "liblzma.so.5.6.1")
    | where SyslogMessage has_any ("sshd", "systemd")
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="Syslog", Host=HostName, Process=ProcessName, Cmd="", File=SyslogMessage;
union edr, aud
| order by TimeGenerated desc
3998.sigma:
title: sshd Loads Backdoored liblzma 5.6.0 / 5.6.1 (CVE-2024-3094)
id: 8b3c1a4e-7d2f-4f9a-9a2c-2b1f5d3c1a4e
status: experimental
description: Detects the OpenSSH daemon loading the malicious liblzma.so.5.6.0 or liblzma.so.5.6.1 introduced by the xz-utils supply chain backdoor (CVE-2024-3094). The backdoor activates when sshd, via libsystemd notification patches, chain-loads the compromised liblzma — at which point the IFUNC crc64_resolve audit hook hijacks RSA_public_decrypt and enables authentication bypass for a holder of the attacker's RSA key.
references:
  - https://snyk.io/blog/the-xz-backdoor-cve-2024-3094/
  - https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2024/03/29/4
  - https://www.sysdig.com/blog/cve-2024-3094-detecting-the-sshd-backdoor-in-xz-utils
  - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-3094
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2024/04/01
tags:
  - attack.t1574.006
  - attack.t1554
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:
  product: linux
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sshd'
      - '/systemd'
  selection_lib:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '/liblzma.so.5.6.0'
      - '/liblzma.so.5.6.1'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_lib
falsepositives:
  - Security research / IR lab hosts intentionally running the backdoored library
  - Snapshot of an older filesystem mounted for forensic review
level: critical
